predecessors.name: Duchy of Württemberg
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Württemberg, 'raised ... to an Electorate' in 1803

predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire (1260-1806)
predecessors.text: the abbeys of Ellwangen, Heiligkreuztal, Rottenmünster, Schöntal and Zwiefalten and the imperial cities of Aalen, Esslingen, Giengen, Heilbronn, Reutlingen, Rottweil, Schwäbisch Gmünd, Schwäbisch…

successors.name: Kingdom of Württemberg
successors.text: the Electorate, enlarged by 'various parts of Further Austria in the Swabian Circle' at Pressburg; 'On 1 January 1806, Duke Frederick III was given the title of King of Württemberg'

ledger.x: 1803: the Imperial Recess raises Württemberg to an electorate.
1803: abbeys and nine imperial cities fall to Württemberg.

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition
wars.outcome: French victory; at Pressburg (26 December 1805) Württemberg received parts of Further Austria in the Swabian Circle and its elector was recognised as King.

certainty.note: The pages name abbeys and cities, not boundary lines; the 1803 acquisitions are scattered enclaves and approximate.
